draft.title: useWorkflowMutation can miss fast workflow completions and stay unresolved
draft.body:
## Summary
`useWorkflowMutation()` relies on WebSocket completion updates after subscribing to an execution. If a workflow reaches terminal state before the completion callback is effectively attached, the hook can remain unresolved even though the execution already finished.

## Current behavior
In `client/src/lib/app-code-platform/useWorkflowMutation.ts`:
- execute workflow
- subscribe to execution updates/logs
- wait for WebSocket completion path

There is no immediate post-subscribe status check to catch executions that completed very quickly.

## Expected behavior
After subscribing, the hook should immediately check execution status once and resolve/reject if the execution is already in a terminal state.

## Why this matters
Fast workflows can complete before the normal completion event is observed by the hook, leaving app-code queries/mutations stuck with no result.

## Likely fix shape
Immediately fetch execution status after subscriptions are stored. If the execution is already terminal (`Success`, `Failed`, `CompletedWithErrors`, `Timeout`, `Cancelled`), resolve or reject the pending deferred state immediately.

## Affected file
- `client/src/lib/app-code-platform/useWorkflowMutation.ts`
draft.author: MTG-Thomas

draft.title: Client retries stale Authorization header after token refresh
draft.body:
## Summary
After a `401`, the frontend refreshes the access token successfully, but then retries the original request with `fetch(request.clone())`. If the original request already carried an `Authorization: Bearer ...` header, the retry reuses the stale token instead of the freshly refreshed one.

## Current behavior
In `client/src/lib/api-client.ts`:
- the client detects `401`
- calls `refreshAccessToken()`
- on success, retries with `fetch(request.clone())`

That replay keeps the old `Authorization` header intact.

## Expected behavior
After a successful refresh, the retried request should rebuild its auth headers from current token state before reissuing the request.

## Why this matters
This can leave the client stuck in an avoidable auth failure path even though refresh succeeded.

## Likely fix shape
Instead of replaying the original cloned request as-is, rebuild the request headers and replace/remove the `Authorization` header using the current token before retry.

## Affected file
- `client/src/lib/api-client.ts`
draft.author: MTG-Thomas

draft.title: [bug]: Summarizer treats OpenRouter 429 as terminal, fails runs permanently
draft.body:
## Summary
`summarize_run` catches all exceptions including `openai.RateLimitError` and permanently marks `summary_status = "failed"`. Transient 429s from the LLM provider (e.g. OpenRouter's 450 RPM cap on gemini-3-flash) are treated identically to invalid JSON or missing config.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Push enough summarization traffic to exceed the provider's RPM limit.
2. Observe worker logs: `openai.RateLimitError: Error code: 429`.
3. Observe affected runs permanently stuck at `summary_status="failed"`.

## Expected behavior
Transient errors (429, 5xx, timeouts) are requeued via RabbitMQ with backoff, not persisted as permanent failures.

## Actual behavior
Every 429 → one permanently failed run. Observed ~689 failures during a backfill this afternoon because the summarizer ran out of retries inside the same rate-limit window.

## Environment
Prod (`bifrost` namespace), worker pods, OpenRouter provider, `google/gemini-3-flash-preview` model.

## Notes
- Code: `api/src/services/execution/run_summarizer.py:255` (the broad `except Exception` that persists failure).
- OpenAI SDK default retries (2) are not enough against a 450 RPM cap being hit by 6 worker pods in parallel.
draft.author: jackmusick

draft.title: [bug]: Backfill summaries publishes all messages at once, thundering-herd LLM provider
draft.body:
## Summary
`POST /api/agent-runs/backfill-summaries` publishes one RabbitMQ message per eligible run in a tight loop, with no throttling. With N worker pods × `max_concurrency` prefetch, a 2000-run backfill instantly saturates the downstream LLM provider's RPM limit.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Trigger a backfill on an agent with ~2000 eligible runs.
2. Watch RabbitMQ: the queue instantly depth-spikes.
3. Watch worker logs: all pods parallel-hit the LLM; most calls 429.

## Expected behavior
Backfills drain serially (one run at a time) or at a rate below the provider's advertised RPM cap. A thousand-run backfill should take minutes of wall time, not burst-fail.

## Actual behavior
Backfill of 1991 runs: ~525 permanently failed before the fleet-wide rate limiter reset (combined with the summarizer never retrying 429).

## Notes
- Code: `api/src/routers/agent_runs.py:1006` (the for-loop publish).
- Consumer: `api/src/jobs/summarize_worker.py` (`SummarizeConsumer` uses `prefetch_count = settings.max_concurrency` × pod count).
- Proposed fix: dedicated `agent-summarization-backfill` queue with a single consumer at `prefetch_count=1`, so the existing `SummaryBackfillJob` orchestration drives a serial drain regardless of worker pod count. Live `agent-summarization` queue stays parallel.

draft.title: [chore]: Auto-deploy to DigitalOcean cluster after main image build
draft.body:
## Summary
After every push to main, the CI `Build Dev Images` job pushes `:dev` tags to GHCR. Today I manually run `kubectl rollout restart` in the cluster to pick them up. Automate this in CI so deploys happen without a human in the loop, and so GitHub's built-in notifications handle the "did it fail?" case.

## Proposed flow
1. Add a `deploy-dev` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that `needs: [build-dev]` and only runs on `push` to `main`.
2. Auth to DigitalOcean with `DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN` secret via `digitalocean/action-doctl`.
3. `doctl kubernetes cluster kubeconfig save <cluster>` to populate kubeconfig.
4. `kubectl -n bifrost rollout restart deployment -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=bifrost`.
5. `kubectl -n bifrost rollout status deployment/<name> --timeout=5m` for each to confirm.
6. Rely on GitHub's built-in workflow-failure email for "deploy broke" notifications.

## Notes
- Target only deployments labeled `app.kubernetes.io/part-of=bifrost` in the `bifrost` namespace, so new services are picked up automatically.
- Skip `bifrost-docs` namespace (separate lifecycle).
- Secrets to add: `DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN` (DO API token, scoped to Kubernetes), `DO_CLUSTER_NAME` (or ID).
- Manual trigger via `workflow_dispatch` so the user can re-deploy without a merge.

## Out of scope
- Success notifications (GitHub only emails on failure by default). Follow-up if that turns out to be annoying.
- Blue/green or canary rollouts — plain `rollout restart` is fine today.

draft.title: [chore]: agent v2 run details polish + captured-data filter
draft.body:
## Summary

Bundle of agent v2 polish items + a new captured-data filter on the runs list. All in one PR since we're iterating fast on this surface.

## 1. Captured Data key/value filter on agent runs list

Filter the runs list by `run_metadata` key/value pairs so we can quickly slice (e.g. `billing_status = Billable AND service_category contains security`).

- **UI**: filter row repeater near the search box on the agent runs list. Each row = key combobox + operator (`eq` / `contains`, default **contains**) + value input. When `op = eq`, value becomes a combobox of known values for that key.
- **Scope**: per-agent only (no global aggregation).
- **Backend**:
  - Extend the existing `metadata_filter` param (`api/src/routers/agent_runs.py:178-194`) from `{k: v}` to `[{key, op, value}]`. Add `.ilike(f"%{v}%")` for `contains`.
  - New `GET /api/agent-runs/metadata-keys?agent_id=…` → distinct top-level keys.
  - New `GET /api/agent-runs/metadata-values?agent_id=…&key=…` → distinct values for that key.
  - GIN index on `AgentRun.metadata` (the DB column for `run_metadata`) — none today (`api/src/models/orm/agent_runs.py:105-113`).
- Pattern reference: `client/src/components/tables/DocumentQueryPanel.tsx:16` for the filter-row repeater.

## 2. Tool calls render as `tool {}` on run details

`RunReviewPanel.tsx` extractor isn't reading the right path. Step content shape is:

```json
{ "type": "llm_response",
  "content": { "tool_calls": [{ "name": "...", "arguments": {...} }] } }
```

Fix `extractToolCalls()` (`client/src/components/agents/RunReviewPanel.tsx:54-76`) to pull `name` from `content.tool_calls[].name` and render it as the row label. Args still on the row but the name is the headline.

## 3. "10 to review" badge is stale / wrong

Frontend computes the count from a 10-run page (`client/src/components/agents/AgentOverviewTab.tsx:55-71`). Backend already exposes the real count as `stats.unreviewed` (`api/src/services/agent_stats.py:73-75`). Switch the badge to use that.

## 4. Run summarizer `did` is generic

Today the prompt has no agent context, so `did` ends up restating the agent's role ("triaged the ticket, assigned categories…"). Two changes in `api/src/services/execution/run_summarizer.py`:

- Pass agent name + system prompt into the user message as context.
- Sharpen `did` instruction: describe the **specific outcome / decisions / entities touched**, not the agent's job. Reference the metadata fields the model already extracts.

## 5. Summary prompt versioning

So we can re-summarize runs that were summarized under an old prompt:

- Add `SUMMARIZE_PROMPT_VERSION = "v2"` constant in `run_summarizer.py` (bump manually when editing the prompt).
- Add `summary_prompt_version: Mapped[str | None]` column to `AgentRun`. **Migration default: `"v1"`** for existing rows.
- Summarizer persists the current version when writing the result.
- Backfill endpoint (`api/src/routers/agent_runs.py:932`) gets a new optional filter `prompt_version_below: str | None` so admins can say "re-summarize anything not on vN."
- (Stretch — not blocking) small badge on the run details panel showing the version.

## Bring back the structured step timeline (NOT in this PR)

The raw-JSON `RawStepTimeline` in `client/src/pages/agents/AgentRunDetailPage.tsx:523-561` is gross but the v1 component (`StepCard` / `stepLabel` / `StepSummary`, removed in `9fdb187870`) is the right replacement and big enough to deserve its own issue. Spinning that out separately.

## Verification

- `./test.sh stack up` then `./test.sh all`
- `cd client && npm run tsc && npm run lint && npm run generate:types`
- `pyright` and `ruff check .` from `api/`
- Manual: agent runs page filter, run details tool-call rendering, dashboard "to review" count, regenerate a run's summary and confirm `summary_prompt_version` populates, run a backfill with the new version filter on a small set.

draft.title: [chore]: skip CI on non-code changes (path filters)
draft.body:
## Summary

CI runs the full suite (Lint & Type, Unit, E2E) on every PR — including ones that only touch markdown, docs, or skill files. With branch protection now requiring all three checks (set 2026-04-25), even doc-only PRs wait ~10min on E2E for no benefit.

Add path filters so heavy jobs skip when only non-code files changed, while keeping branch protection happy.

## Approach

Add `paths-ignore` to the `pull_request` trigger of the heavy jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (or wherever Unit/E2E live):

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - '**/*.md'
      - '.claude/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - '.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**'
```

## Branch-protection gotcha

A workflow that *didn't run* is not the same as one that *passed*. With `Unit Tests` listed as a required check, a doc-only PR will be permanently `BLOCKED` because the required check never reports.

**Fix:** the canonical pattern is a "skip shim" — a tiny job that runs ONLY when the heavy job is skipped, reports a green status with the same name, and unblocks the PR. Two options:

1. **GitHub-native shim:** for each required check, add a paired job named identically that runs on the inverse path filter and immediately exits 0. GitHub's UI shows the shim's status for the required-check name.
2. **Single "always-pass" gating job:** rename the required check to something like `CI Gate`, make it a single workflow that fans out to lint/unit/e2e via `needs:`, and condition the heavy needs on path filters. Branch protection only requires `CI Gate`, which always runs.

Option 2 is cleaner long-term but is a larger workflow refactor. Option 1 is more mechanical and lower risk.

## Keep `Lint & Type Check` on every PR

It's fast (~2-3min) and catches markdown formatting / link issues. Only Unit Tests and E2E Tests should be path-gated.

## Verification

- [ ] Open a doc-only PR (e.g. tweak `.claude/skills/bifrost-issues/SKILL.md`), confirm Unit + E2E skip.
- [ ] Branch protection still allows the PR to merge (no permanent `BLOCKED`).
- [ ] Open a normal code PR, confirm all three jobs run.
- [ ] Confirm `Lint & Type Check` still runs on doc-only PRs.

## Notes

- Files: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (likely; verify the actual workflow file)
- Branch protection contexts: `Lint & Type Check`, `Unit Tests`, `E2E Tests`
- Triggered by: PR #38 took ~10min on doc-only commits to `.claude/skills/`

draft.title: [chore]: code-fix sweep for react-hooks 7.1 / eslint 10 expanded recommended set
draft.body:
## Background

`eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.1` and `eslint@10` ship an expanded recommended preset that adds:

- `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` — `setState` calls in effect bodies (~40 sites)
- `react-hooks/refs` — ref access during render (~6 sites)
- `react-hooks/immutability` — direct mutation of state (~3 sites)
- `react-hooks/incompatible-library` — hooks called in incompatible contexts (~2 sites)
- `react-hooks/error-boundaries` — bad error boundary patterns (~1 site)
- `@eslint/js`'s `preserve-caught-error` — rethrows that lose `cause` (~8 sites)
- `no-useless-assignment` (~1 site)

Total: ~60 lint errors across ~30 files.

These are real signals, not noise — silencing them in eslint config would be a regression.

## Why this is being filed now

PR #72 (the npm minor-and-patch group bump) included `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` 7.0.1 → 7.1.1, which surfaced these errors and broke its CI. PR #73 added an ignore rule pinning the plugin at 7.0.x until this sweep lands.

PRs #61 (eslint 10) and #65 (typescript 6) were also closed for related reasons — both blocked on upstream peer-dep tightening.

## Scope

- Fix all current call sites (the list will be re-derived once we install plugin 7.1+ in a worktree)
- Where a `setState` in an effect is intentional (e.g., syncing external state), use the `set-state-in-effect`-suppressed pattern documented in the plugin (typically `useSyncExternalStore` or a callback ref)
- Where a `setState` is a code smell (cascading render), refactor to derive the state from props or memo
- For `preserve-caught-error`, add `cause` to rethrown errors
- For `react-hooks/refs`, move ref reads into effects or event handlers
- After fixing, remove the ignore rule for `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` and `eslint-plugin-react-refresh` from `.github/dependabot.yml` and let Dependabot land the bumps

## Estimated effort

~1 day of focused work. The fixes are mostly mechanical per category but require reading each effect to confirm the pattern.

## Acceptance

- `npm run lint` passes with `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@^7.1` and `eslint-plugin-react-refresh@^0.5` installed in a worktree
- Eslint 10 also passes (verify in same worktree by bumping `eslint` and `@eslint/js` to 10)
- Dependabot ignore rules lifted in a follow-up PR

draft.title: [bug]: ./test.sh E2E flakes with 'stack not running for this worktree' immediately after 'Stack is up'
draft.body:
## Summary

The E2E job in CI (`./test.sh client e2e`) intermittently fails with this exact pattern:

\`\`\`
Stack is up. Project: bifrost-test-0b7397c6
ERROR: stack not running for this worktree. Run:
  ./test.sh stack up
\`\`\`

Note that "Stack is up" prints on the line BEFORE the "not running" error. The script registers the stack, then in its very next check, doesn't see it.

## Where seen

- PR #84 fix/empty-except-cleanup, run 24940923661 (E2E job 73034432074) — failed at 21:36 UTC
- Almost certainly the cause of several other "FAILURE" runs across the auto-merge queue today

A simple `gh run rerun --failed` typically passes on retry.

## Hypothesis

`./test.sh` has a race between the stack startup (\`docker-compose up\` + healthcheck wait) and the subsequent stack-status check. The compose project name registration may not be visible to the next shell command immediately.

## Repro

Run `./test.sh client e2e` repeatedly in CI; should hit this once every ~10-20 runs based on today's evidence.

## Fix ideas

- Add a short \`docker compose ls\` poll/sleep loop in the stack-status check
- Or: query the project name via Docker SDK rather than CLI shellout
- Or: hold an explicit FD/lockfile through both phases

## Impact

Mid-priority. Doesn't break correctness; does cause spurious CI churn (re-runs needed) and obscures real failures behind flake noise. Today this caused ~4 hours of confusion about whether PRs were actually broken.

draft.title: [feature]: External MCP Client — agents can call tools on registered external MCP servers
draft.body:
### Problem

`resolve_agent_tools()` builds an agent's toolset from three local sources today (system, workflows, delegation) — all in-process Python. No way to call a tool on an external MCP server. With the MCP ecosystem expanding fast (M365, Slack, Atlassian, vendor servers, custom), the only options for an operator are mirror-each-as-a-workflow (doesn't scale) or skip Bifrost and use Claude Desktop / Code directly. Asymmetric with the existing direction since Bifrost already *serves* MCP — adding the *client* side is the natural complement. SpireTech has a concrete forcing example (an MCP server fronting HaloPSA), but the design is generic.

**First question — is this already planned?** If you've got something in flight or a different shape in mind, point me at it.

### Proposed solution

Reuse `integrations` + `oauth_providers` + `configs`, add a `kind` discriminator and one new `external_mcp_tools` cache table. Per-agent grants follow the existing tool-grant model (same picker, same UX). `resolve_agent_tools()` gains a fourth source. Executor branches on tool kind — workflows still in-process, external MCP tools dispatch via a new MCP client wrapper. Two-layer access control: Bifrost grants AND remote server scopes; either can deny.

Full design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-25-external-mcp-client-design.md`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admin registers an `external_mcp` integration via existing Integrations UI (URL + OAuth client_credentials)
- [ ] On save, Bifrost validates connectivity, fetches `tools/list`, populates the catalog
- [ ] Granting an external MCP tool to an agent works identically to granting a workflow tool, same picker
- [ ] Agent runs pick up granted external tools; LLM can invoke them; results route through the standard envelope
- [ ] Audit log records `(agent_run_id, integration_id, tool_name, status, duration)`
- [ ] Per-tool result size cap and wall-clock timeout enforced; per-integration overrides
- [ ] Unit + e2e + Playwright tests per CONTRIBUTING.md
- [ ] Migration reversible; existing integrations (`kind=standard` default) unaffected

### Design doc link

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-25-external-mcp-client-design.md`

draft.title: test flake: test_schedule_promote_run_terminal timing race ('expected at least 1 promoted row, got 0')
draft.body:
## Symptom

`api/tests/e2e/api/test_workflow_scheduling_flow.py::test_schedule_promote_run_terminal` fails intermittently with:

```
AssertionError: expected at least 1 promoted row, got 0
```

## Suspected root cause

Test creates a scheduled execution and polls for it to be promoted by the scheduler. The poll is timing-sensitive — if the scheduler is busy or slow on the test runner, the poll times out before promotion happens.

## Fix sketch

Two options:

1. **Quick:** bump the polling timeout. Hides the flake but doesn't fix the underlying race.
2. **Correct:** wait for the scheduler to acknowledge the scheduled execution before checking promotion. Requires either:
   - The scheduler exposing a 'ready' signal we can subscribe to
   - Adding such a signal if it doesn't exist

Option 2 is the right fix.

## Reference
Saw this on runs: 24943992176, 24943705451 during the 2026-04-25 OSS hardening session

## Done when
- Test passes 100/100 sequential runs
- Either uses a real readiness signal from the scheduler OR has a justified timeout with rationale in code

draft.title: RFC: scan findings lifecycle primitive for external security signals
draft.body:
## RFC

This is a request for direction before treating the accompanying implementation as a normal feature PR.

Bifrost already has workflows, org-scoped storage, apps, and operator-facing execution history. One reusable capability that seems adjacent to that vision is a small platform primitive for recurring external observations: ingest results from an external scanner, track each run, deduplicate repeated observations, resolve observations that disappear in later runs, and let operators transition finding state.

The prototype branch uses Nuclei as the first concrete producer because its output is structured and repeatable. The intended platform question is broader than Nuclei:

> Should Bifrost have a first-class scan/finding lifecycle API for external security or compliance signals, or should this remain workspace-specific code built only on tables/workflows?

## Prototype shape

The draft implementation adds an admin-only FastAPI router under `/api/scans/*` that stores data in existing org-scoped table documents instead of introducing new database tables.

It includes:

- scan run creation and history
- Nuclei finding ingestion
- severity validation
- occurrence-key hashing
- re-alert suppression for already open or acknowledged findings
- resolve-on-absence behavior for scanned hosts
- incomplete-run handling
- findings filtering by state, severity, and template tag
- bulk finding state transitions

## Why this might fit upstream

- It is a reusable lifecycle primitive for workflow-produced or externally produced findings, not an MSP-specific ticketing flow.
- It gives Bifrost apps and workflows a consistent backend surface for recurring scan observations.
- It avoids schema/migration overhead for the first slice by using the existing table/document store.
- It leaves downstream policy decisions, PSA tickets, and reporting in workspace code.

## Open questions

- Should the API remain Nuclei-specific for an initial concrete slice, or be generalized first to `security_findings` / `scanner_findings`?
- Should this stay as a thin router over existing tables, or move to explicit contracts/service modules before merge?
- Is admin-only access the right initial permission model?
- Is resolve-on-absence appropriate as default behavior, or should it be opt-in per scan run?

draft.title: Execution hardening: webhook rate limits, schedule overlap, stuck-execution fix
draft.body:
## Problem

The execution system is a single shared FIFO pool fed by multiple trigger sources (apps, agents, schedules, webhooks). One noisy source — a service provider auto-replying 100 emails into the ticketing queue — can saturate the pool, starving everything else, including a one-second list query from an app loading data.

When operators react by mass-cancelling, executions that were already mid-route can sit in the database with `status=RUNNING` for 15+ minutes before the cleanup reaper notices, even with the queue otherwise empty.

## Scope

Three independent changes shipped together. Each is independently mergeable.

1. **Per-source webhook rate limiting** at the `/api/hooks/{source_id}` ingress. Sliding-window limiter (reuses `core/rate_limit.py`), 60/min default, per-source configurable, returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Stops storms at the door before any `Event` / `EventDelivery` rows are written.
2. **Schedule overlap policy** on `ScheduleSource` — `skip` / `queue` / `replace` enum, only `skip` implemented in v1. Schedules don't pile up new copies when the previous run is still in flight. Webhooks deliberately do *not* get an overlap check: every webhook carries unique payload and silently dropping one is a correctness bug. Source rate limit handles the webhook story; overlap policy handles the schedule story; they don't share columns or code.
3. **Stuck-execution bug fix** — when a worker process dies silently, `process_pool.py:_check_process_health` now fires the result callback immediately so the DB status flips to `FAILED` within seconds instead of 15+ minutes (currently waits for the 5-min `execution_cleanup` reaper after `timeout_seconds + 5min grace`).

## Out of scope (separate specs)

- Per-agent concurrency caps
- `queue` / `replace` overlap policies (column added now, behavior is follow-up)
- Cost ceilings, per-org quotas, event dedup keys, circuit breakers
- Bulk-cancel UI
- Priority lanes / reserved pool capacity (the throttles in this spec prevent the saturation that would make priority lanes necessary)

## Design doc

[`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-execution-hardening-rate-limits-design.md`](https://github.com/jackmusick/bifrost/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-execution-hardening-rate-limits-design.md)

## Suggested merge order

1. Stuck-execution fix (no schema change, purely additive, biggest immediate operator pain)
2. Schedule overlap (one column, ships with `skip` enabled by default)
3. Webhook rate limiting (largest surface: model, migration, handler refactor, UI)

draft.title: chore: per-worktree debug stacks + bifrost-debug skill, fix seed-user provisioning
draft.body:
## Summary

Today `./debug.sh` is not worktree-isolated (single `bifrost-dev` Compose project, fixed host ports), so only one worktree can run a dev stack at a time. Working on multiple feature branches in parallel requires constantly stopping and starting the stack.

This change makes `debug.sh` mirror `test.sh`: per-worktree Compose project name, two boot modes (Netbird sidecar when a setup key is present, otherwise auto-allocated host port for the client only), and verb-style subcommands (`up`/`down`/`status`/`logs`). Adds a new `bifrost-debug` skill that teaches Claude how to bring up an isolated stack on demand.

Also fixes a related bug: `BIFROST_DEFAULT_USER_EMAIL` / `BIFROST_DEFAULT_USER_PASSWORD` create a User row but no Organization, so `has_users()` (which requires `organization_id IS NOT NULL`) returns false, the setup wizard appears, and registration fails with "user already exists." The seeded account is in a dead-end state — can't log in, can't complete setup.

## Scope

- Rewrite `debug.sh` with verb subcommands; new `docker-compose.debug.yml`.
- Per-worktree Compose project name (re-use `compute_project_name` from `scripts/lib/test_helpers.sh`).
- Mode A (Netbird): sidecar shares client's network namespace, hostname is worktree-derived. Setup key from `~/.config/bifrost/debug.env` (per-user, gitignored) or process env.
- Mode B (no Netbird): auto-pick free host port, expose client only.
- New checked-in `.env.debug`: `dev@gobifrost.com` / `password`, MFA off.
- Fix `create_default_user()` in `api/src/main.py` to call `ensure_user_provisioned()`, set `is_registered=True` and `mfa_enabled=False` so the seeded user is fully provisioned.
- New `.claude/skills/bifrost-debug/SKILL.md`. Updates to `bifrost-issues` (drop "only one debug.sh" warning, reference new skill) and `bifrost-testing` (point UI-click-around steps at new skill).

## Out of scope

- HTTPS / Netbird reverse-proxy config (one-time manual step in Netbird Admin).
- Auto-provisioning Netbird PAT or rotating keys.
- Touching `bifrost-demo` setup — separate.
- SessionEnd hook lifecycle automation — explicitly avoided per design discussion.

## Acceptance

- Two worktrees can run `./debug.sh up` simultaneously without colliding.
- In Netbird mode: stack URL is reachable via the worktree-derived peer hostname; login as `dev@gobifrost.com / password` works without setup wizard or MFA prompt.
- In port-allocation mode: same login, URL is `http://localhost:<auto-port>`.
- `bifrost-issues` skill no longer warns about cross-worktree debug.sh conflicts.

draft.title: [feature]: Chat V2 / Phase 1 / M1 — Workspaces foundations
draft.body:
**Part of #139** (Phase 1 tracking).
**Spec reference:** \`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-chat-ux-design.md\` — §2 (Workspaces), §11 (Data model), §12 (M1 milestone), §16.1-16.3 (UX descriptions).
**Estimated effort:** ~1.5 weeks.

## Summary

Introduce **workspaces** as a first-class scoping construct that conversations belong to. Mirrors the existing forms/agents/workflows scoping model (personal / org / role). The synthetic \"Personal\" workspace is auto-created per user. Sidebar primary nav gains a Workspaces destination; entering a workspace re-scopes the chat surface (sidebar shows workspace's chats; right rail shows workspace context). No model-resolver, attachments, edit/retry, or other features yet — just the foundation.

## Scope

### Backend

- New ORM table \`workspaces\` with fields:
  - \`id\` (UUID), \`name\`, \`description\`
  - \`scope\` (enum: \`personal\` / \`org\` / \`role\`), \`role_id\`, \`org_id\`, \`user_id\`
  - \`default_agent_id\` (nullable)
  - \`enabled_tool_ids\` (JSONB list, nullable — null = no restriction)
  - \`enabled_knowledge_source_ids\` (JSONB list, nullable)
  - \`instructions\` (text, nullable)
  - \`is_active\` (soft-delete), \`created_by\`, \`created_at\`, \`updated_at\`
- Add \`workspace_id\` (UUID NOT NULL FK) to \`conversations\` with default backfill to user's Personal workspace.
- Auto-create a Personal workspace per user on first chat access (idempotent).
- New REST endpoints under \`/api/workspaces\`: list / get / create / update / soft-delete. Permissions match existing org/role model.
- Tool intersection rule when assembling context for chats in a workspace: \`agent.tool_ids ∩ workspace.enabled_tool_ids\` (workspace can restrict but never expand).

### Frontend

- New service module \`client/src/services/workspaceService.ts\`.
- Sidebar refactor (per §16.1):
  - Top primary nav block: \`+ New chat\`, \`Workspaces\`, \`Artifacts\` (placeholder, sub-project (4)), \`Customize\` (placeholder).
  - Search input.
  - Pinned section (placeholder UI; pinning logic lands in M7).
  - Recent section (flat chat list).
  - User block at bottom.
- Workspace list page (basic — full design comes in workspace mode).
- Workspace mode (per §16.2): sidebar re-scopes when user enters a workspace. Right rail with workspace context.
- Workspace settings Sheet (per §16.3): General / Tools / Knowledge / Instructions tabs.
- Conversation creation always assigns a \`workspace_id\` (defaults to current workspace if in workspace mode, else Personal).

## Out of scope (this issue)

Deferred to later milestones in this phase:
- Model resolver and per-workspace model allowlists (M2)
- Per-conversation instructions, edit, retry (M3)
- Attachments (M4)
- Compaction (M5)
- Multi-agent delegation in chat (M6)
- Sidebar search, rename, export, cost-tier badges, floating composer polish (M7)

Workspace UI in M1 ships with the floating composer — but the polished cost-tier badges, etc. are M7.

## Data migration plan

Single Alembic migration:
1. Create \`workspaces\` table.
2. Add \`workspace_id\` column to \`conversations\` (NOT NULL with server_default = synthetic Personal workspace id, then drop the default after backfill).
3. For each user with conversations, create a Personal workspace and assign their existing conversations to it.

Migration is run by the \`bifrost-init\` container. After applying, restart \`bifrost-dev-api-1\` to pick up the new schema.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Backend tests: workspace CRUD, scope enforcement, tool intersection.
- [ ] Existing chat E2E tests still pass with conversations now belonging to a Personal workspace.
- [ ] User can create / rename / soft-delete a workspace through the UI.
- [ ] Conversations created from within a workspace land in that workspace.
- [ ] Workspace mode re-scopes the sidebar correctly.
- [ ] All Bifrost pre-completion checks pass (\`pyright\`, \`ruff check\`, \`npm run tsc\`, \`npm run lint\`, \`./test.sh all\`, \`./test.sh client unit\`).

## Implementation notes

- Use \`./debug.sh\` in this issue's worktree for UI development (per-worktree dev stacks are now isolated — see \`bifrost-debug\` skill).
- Type generation: after API changes, run \`npm run generate:types\` in the worktree's client dir while the worktree's dev stack is up.
- Touchpoint files (non-exhaustive):
  - \`api/src/models/orm/agents.py\` (Conversation gains \`workspace_id\`)

draft.title: [feature]: Per-app Tailwind compilation in the v2 app bundler (arbitrary values, @apply, @layer, per-app config)
draft.body:
## Problem

The v2 app bundler does not run Tailwind against per-app source. The host preloads a single Tailwind stylesheet compiled from the host's own files (`client/src/**`), so any class string an app writes that the host's compiler didn't see at host-build time silently no-ops at render. App authors hit this constantly without warning:

- Arbitrary values silently fail: `max-w-[1400px]`, `bg-[color:var(--paper)]`, `lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_360px]`, `min-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)]`, `px-[clamp(1rem,3vw,2.5rem)]`.
- `@apply` in app `styles.css` passes through verbatim — esbuild's CSS loader doesn't process Tailwind directives, so the browser rejects it.
- `@layer components { .x { @apply ... } }` doesn't work for the same reason.
- Per-app `tailwind.config.{ts,js,mjs,cjs}` is ignored entirely; apps can't extend the theme with custom tokens.

Real production apps already exhibit this: `customer-onboarding` uses `w-[500px]` (`pages/index.tsx:288`, skeleton loader width) and `text-[10px]` (`components/OnboardingPipeline.tsx:292`, label sizing) — both classes are in the DOM but no CSS rule fires, so they render at fallback widths/sizes. The Pipeline Command session in the demo workspace lost ~2 hours to this exact category of silent visual breakage (side rail at bottom from `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_360px]`, translucent drawer from `bg-[color:var(--paper)]`, missing page padding from `py-10 lg:py-14`).

The cumulative effect is "second-class app builder": developers (and Claude) must remember a list of Tailwind features that don't work in Bifrost, and that list is exactly the long-tail features people reach for in modern shadcn-style apps.

## Proposed solution

Wire the existing `@tailwindcss/node` v4 compiler (already in the repo, used by the legacy per-file `app_compiler` path) into the modern bundler in two phases:

**Phase 1**: per-app utility compilation. Bundler scans every materialized `.tsx/.ts/.jsx/.js` source for class candidates, asks `@tailwindcss/node` to compile them, writes the output to `__bifrost_tailwind.css`, sorts it ahead of user CSS in the synthesized entry. Bumps `SCHEMA_VERSION` so existing apps rebuild on first viewer request after deploy.

**Phase 2**: full pipeline. `tailwind.js` gains a "pipeline" mode that also takes user CSS files (concatenated into the Tailwind input so `@apply` / `@layer` / `@theme` are processed) and an optional per-app config path (threaded as `@config`). Bundler reads `.css` files, detects `tailwind.config.{ts,js,mjs,cjs}`, and removes consumed user CSS from the entry's import list (since they're now inlined into the unified output — re-importing through esbuild would either duplicate CSS or, for `@apply`-bearing files, fail).

Strictly additive at the runtime layer: standard utilities still come from the host preload; the per-app stylesheet just fills in the long tail. Cascade order is correct (utilities first, user CSS overrides).

Two pre-existing bugs in the candidate extractor surface during this work and are fixed: token splitter was splitting on `,` (broke `minmax(0,1fr)`), and the class-shape regex rejected `(` and `)` (broke `var()`, `calc()`, `clamp()`, `oklch()`). Bugs predated this change, hidden behind the host preload.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_360px]`, `bg-[color:var(--x)]`, `max-w-[1400px]`, `min-h-[calc(100vh-4rem)]`, `px-[clamp(1rem,3vw,2.5rem)]` compile to real CSS rules in the bundle output
- [ ] `@apply` in app `styles.css` produces real declarations (no `@apply` directive remains in output)
- [ ] `@apply` with arbitrary values works (`@apply bg-[color:var(--x)]`)
- [ ] `@layer components { .x { @apply ... } }` is preserved as a layer with the chain expanded
- [ ] Per-app `tailwind.config.{ts,js,mjs,cjs}` with `theme.extend.colors.brand.500` causes `bg-brand-500` to compile with the custom color
- [ ] `:root { --x: ... }` and `.dark { ... }` selectors in user CSS pass through unchanged
- [ ] `customer-onboarding` re-bundles with no behavior regression for its existing standard utilities (`h-full`, `overflow-hidden`, etc.)
- [ ] `customer-onboarding`'s previously-broken `w-[500px]` and `text-[10px]` now compile
- [ ] `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped so deployed apps rebuild on first viewer request after deploy (no manual republish)
- [ ] Integration tests against the real `@tailwindcss/node` subprocess cover all of the above
- [ ] All existing bundler + compiler tests still pass

## Design doc link (optional)

docs/experiments/v2-tailwind-quickwin.md

draft.title: [feature]: Chat V2 / Phase 1 / M2 — Model resolver + curation
draft.body:
Second milestone of Chat V2 / Phase 1. Lands the **shared model resolver**, a **`platform_models` DB table** populated by a background job that fetches a checked-in `models.json` from GitHub raw on an interval (so fresh models reach running installs without a redeploy), and the **picker UI** with provenance tooltips.

Targets the long-lived integration branch `feature/chat-v2`, stacking on top of M1 (#140, merged in #144).

## Read first
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-27-chat-v2-master-plan.md` — orchestration; "Cross-program follow-ups" table folds two deferred items into this milestone (capability matrix, per-user default).
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-chat-ux-design.md` §5 (model resolver), §11.1/§11.2 (data model), §12 M2.

## How the registry stays fresh

```
GitHub Action (in this repo, separate follow-up) → calls OpenRouter → commits api/shared/data/models.json
                                                                            ↓
                                                                  (normal commit to main)
                                                                            ↓
Bifrost install fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jackmusick/bifrost/main/api/shared/data/models.json
                          on an interval (every N hours, ETag-aware)
                                                                            ↓
                                                       Upserts platform_models DB table
                                                                            ↓
                                              Resolver / picker / org allowlist all query the table
```

**Key properties:**
- **No redeploy needed** — running installs pull the file from GitHub raw on a schedule.
- **Air-gapped / first-boot still works** — the same file is also checked into the repo, so the install has a working seed even if it can't reach GitHub.
- **No external runtime dependency on OpenRouter from production** — the Action talks to OpenRouter, installs never do.
- **No SaaS catalog to host** — the repo is the catalog.

The GitHub Action that publishes the file is **out of M2 scope** — M2 ships with a hand-curated seed `models.json` plus the consumer-side machinery; the Action can land later.

## Resolver chain

Two layers of restriction (global table + optional org), then defaults cascade most-specific-wins:

```
platform_models (synced from models.json)   ← global catalog of supported models
       ↓ intersect (optional)
orgs.allowed_chat_models                    ← admin's optional further narrowing
       ↓ then defaults cascade
org → role → workspace → user → conversation → message
```

Roles, workspaces, and users only set defaults — not allowlists.

## Scope

### Backend

**`api/shared/model_resolver.py`**
- `resolve_model(context: ModelResolutionContext) -> ModelChoice` — walks the chain above.
- Applies alias resolution (`bifrost-fast` / `bifrost-balanced` / `bifrost-premium`) and deprecation remap at lookup time.
- `Message.model` is **never remapped** — immutable history (spec §5.8.4).
- Capability check helper: `pick_compatible(allowed_models, required_capabilities) -> str | None`.

**`platform_models` table**
- Columns: `model_id` (PK), `provider`, `display_name`, `capabilities` (JSONB: `supports_images_in`, `supports_images_out`, `supports_pdf_in`, `supports_tool_use`, `supports_audio_in`, `supports_audio_out`), `cost_tier`, `context_window`, `max_output_tokens`, `pricing` (JSONB), `created_at`, `updated_at`.

**`api/shared/data/models.json`**
- Checked-in seed. Hand-curated for M2 (the Action that auto-publishes from OpenRouter is a follow-up).
- Pydantic schema validates on load.

**Background sync job**
- Interval (every N hours, configurable; also on startup if the table is empty).
- Fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jackmusick/bifrost/main/api/shared/data/models.json` with `If-None-Match` (ETag).
- On 200: upserts `platform_models` from the response. Models missing from the file are deactivated/removed.
- On 304: no-op.
- On network failure: leave existing rows alone, log warning.
- On first boot with no network: seed from the bundled file shipped in the repo.
- Configurable URL via env var so self-hosters can point at a fork or a private mirror.

**Save-time orphan-reference audit (spec §5.8.5)**
- When admin removes a model from `orgs.allowed_chat_models`, scan workspaces / roles / users / conversations / agents for references.
- Show remediation modal: "Saving will orphan N references — choose replacements". Suggest closest available model in same `cost_tier`. Idempotent.
- API: `POST /api/admin/models/migrate-references` per spec §5.8.5.

**Aliases & deprecation tables**
- `org_model_aliases` (per spec §5.8.1) — DB table, org-scoped.
- `model_deprecations` — populated from `models.json` (platform-wide entries) plus org-level overrides in DB.

**ORM additions**
- `users.default_chat_model VARCHAR NULL` — per-user default (no allowlist).
- `roles.default_chat_model VARCHAR NULL`.
- `workspaces.default_model VARCHAR NULL` (verify whether M1 already added it).
- `orgs.allowed_chat_models JSONB DEFAULT '[]'` + `orgs.default_chat_model VARCHAR NULL`.
- `conversations.current_model VARCHAR NULL`.
- `messages.cost_tier VARCHAR NULL`.

**Wire resolver into `agent_executor.py`** for chat turns. Summarization call site lands in M5; resolver is built ready for it.

### Capability handling

1. **User attaches an image, picked model lacks `supports_images_in`** — composer shows inline warning before send. User decides; no silent reroute.
2. **User asks the model to generate an image, picked model lacks `supports_images_out`** — let the model refuse; surface its response.
3. **A tool requires a capability the picked model lacks** — tool shows disabled in tools panel with explanatory tooltip.

### Frontend

- **Chat picker UI (spec §16.6)** — visible-but-disabled provenance tooltips, cost-tier glyphs (⚡ / ⚖ / 💎), sets `conversations.current_model`.
- **Per-message override hook on the retry dropdown** — data plumbing only; UI in M3.
- **User-level "Default model"** in user preferences.
- **Org admin allowlist + default-model controls** added to the existing org settings page (no new platform admin Models page — the registry is sourced from a file, nothing to edit at runtime).

## Acceptance criteria

- `resolve_model()` unit-tested across every chain level: platform-only, org-narrowed, role-default, workspace-default, user-default, conversation-override, message-override, alias-follow, deprecation-remap, capability-fallback.
- Sync job covered by unit + e2e tests: 200 → upsert (new + updated rows), 304 → no-op, network failure → leave existing rows, removed-from-file → row removed, first-boot empty table → seed from bundled file.
- Picker shows provenance tooltips and tier glyphs end-to-end (vitest + Playwright).
- Capability pre-flight utility (`check_message_compat(content_blocks, model_id)`) unit-tested against the registry for image-in / pdf-in / tool-use cases. The composer wiring + Playwright coverage lands in M4 once attachments exist.
- Save-time orphan audit: removing a model from org allowlist with active references opens the remediation modal; applying it dual-writes (rows + deprecation entry) per spec §5.8.5.
- Pre-completion verification: `pyright`, `ruff`, `npm run tsc`, `npm run lint`, `./test.sh all`, `./test.sh client unit`, `./test.sh client e2e` — all green.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- The GitHub Action that publishes `models.json` from OpenRouter — separate follow-up issue.
- Admin-editable platform registry — superseded by file-sourced approach.
- Display-name overrides per spec §5.8.6 — lands with M7.
- Org admin AI settings page (spec §16.7) full implementation — M7; M2 only ships the allowlist + default-model controls.
- Models not in OpenRouter's catalog (internal / self-hosted endpoints not proxied through OpenRouter) — add later if real demand surfaces.

## Branching

- Worktree: `.worktrees/145-model-resolver`.
- Branch: `145-model-resolver`, based on `origin/feature/chat-v2`.
- PR opens **into `feature/chat-v2`**, not `main`.

## Tracks
Part of #139 (Phase 1 tracking).

draft.title: [feature]: Chat V2 / Phase 1 / M3 — Edit, retry, per-conversation instructions (with branching)
draft.body:
## Goal
Ship M3 of the Chat V2 / Phase 1 Chat UX overhaul: edit, retry, and per-conversation instructions — built on top of message branching so edits and retries are non-destructive (matching Claude.ai / ChatGPT / LibreChat / Open WebUI).

## What's in this milestone

### Backend
- Migration: `Message.parent_message_id UUID NULL FK messages.id`, `Conversation.active_leaf_message_id UUID NULL FK messages.id`, `Conversation.instructions TEXT NULL`. Backfill `parent_message_id` from `sequence` for existing rows; backfill `active_leaf_message_id` to the last message of each conversation.
- `agent_executor._build_message_history` walks `active_leaf_message_id` → root via `parent_message_id` instead of `ORDER BY sequence`. Tool-call ID remap logic stays (operates on the resolved linear path).
- New endpoint `POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages/{msg_id}/edit` — creates a sibling user message under the same parent, sets new active leaf, dispatches a turn.
- New endpoint `POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages/{msg_id}/retry` — creates a sibling assistant message under the same parent, sets new active leaf, dispatches a turn.
- New endpoint `PATCH /api/conversations/{id}/active-leaf` — switches active leaf (sibling navigation).
- New endpoint `PATCH /api/conversations/{id}` accepts `instructions` field. System prompt assembly in `_build_message_history` appends `conversation.instructions` after agent prompt + workspace instructions.

### Frontend
- Pencil hover icon on user message bubbles → inline editable textarea + Save/Cancel. Save creates a sibling and switches active leaf.
- RotateCcw hover icon on assistant message bubbles → single-click retry creates a sibling.
- Sibling navigation: `< 2/3 >` arrows on any message that has siblings. Arrows update active leaf; chat re-renders the active path.
- Conversation header overflow → "Customize this chat" Dialog with autosize textarea + live token cost preview. Save persists `Conversation.instructions`.
- Chat store: branch-aware message rendering (flat array of the active path, derived from `active_leaf_message_id`), `editMessage`, `retryMessage`, `switchBranch` actions.

### Spec updates (in this PR)
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-chat-ux-design.md`:
  - §1.1: replace "no branching" with branching-on-edit semantics.
  - §1.2: drop "Switching models via retry sets the conversation's current model" + drop the model override dropdown.
  - §16.9: drop AlertDialog confirm.
  - §16.10: drop the Popover-with-ModelPicker; just a RotateCcw button.
  - Non-goals: remove "Branching/tree conversations (linear-only)."
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-27-chat-v2-master-plan.md`: add a note in the decisions log.

### Out of scope
- Retry-with-different-model dropdown.
- Compaction-aware branch handling (M5's problem).
- Branch-aware export (v1 exports active branch only — already correct).

## Tests
- Unit: `test_message_history_branching.py` — parent-chain walk, sibling resolution, active-leaf switching, edit creates sibling, retry creates sibling.
- E2E (`api/tests/e2e/`): edit creates new branch + dispatches turn; retry creates new branch + dispatches turn; PATCH instructions persists and shows up in next turn's system prompt; sibling switch endpoint.
- Vitest: chatStore branch-aware path resolution; editMessage/retryMessage/switchBranch reducers; instructions dialog component.
- Playwright: edit a user message and confirm both branches accessible via arrows; retry an assistant message and switch back; set per-conversation instructions and confirm next response reflects them.

## Branching strategy
- PR target: `feature/chat-v2` (NOT main).
- Worktree at `.worktrees/<issue#>-m3-edit-retry-instructions/`.
- Branched from `origin/feature/chat-v2`, not main.

## Closes
This issue closes when M3 ships into `feature/chat-v2`. The phase-1 tracking issue (#139) stays open.

draft.title: manifest sync: integration UUID rewrite collides with FK CASCADE on integration_config_schema
draft.body:
## Summary

Manifest sync fails with a `UniqueViolationError` on `ix_integration_config_schema_unique_key` when an `Integration` row's UUID gets rewritten (existing-by-name match in `_resolve_integration`).

## Repro

1. Have an `Integration` in the DB with UUID **A** and name `"Foo"`, with config_schema rows referencing integration_id = A.
2. Update `.bifrost/integrations.yaml` so `"Foo"` has UUID **B** (different).
3. Run `POST /api/github/sync`.
4. Sync fails with:
   ```
   sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.asyncpg.IntegrityError: <class 'asyncpg.exceptions.UniqueViolationError'>
   duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ix_integration_config_schema_unique_key"
   DETAIL: Key (integration_id, key)=(B, <some_key>) already exists.
   [SQL: INSERT INTO integration_config_schema ...]
   ```

## Root cause

In `api/src/services/manifest_import.py` in `_resolve_integration`:

1. **Line ~1766–1780** — when `existing_by_name` matches, an `Upsert` is built that rewrites the integration's `id` from A to B. SQLAlchemy emits an `UPDATE integrations SET id = B WHERE id = A`.
2. **Postgres FK** on `integration_config_schema.integration_id` is `ON UPDATE CASCADE`. The cascade migrates schema rows from A → B *during the same statement*.
3. **Line 1786** — the cache lookup is keyed on `integ_id` (the manifest UUID, B), but **the cache was populated before the upsert ran**, so it has schema rows under A, not B. Lookup at B returns `{}`.
4. **Line 1796–1814** — the loop doesn't see existing rows under B, takes the `else` branch, and tries to `INSERT` a new schema row at `(B, key)`. But CASCADE already migrated rows there → unique constraint violation.

```python
# Line 1785-1793 — cache lookup uses the NEW integ_id
if cache is not None:
    existing_cs_by_key = dict(cache["integ_cs"].get(integ_id, {}))  # integ_id = B
else:
    existing_cs_result = await self.db.execute(
        select(IntegrationConfigSchema).where(
            IntegrationConfigSchema.integration_id == integ_id  # B
        )
    )
    ...
```

The non-cache branch (else) actually works correctly because it queries the DB *after* the upsert + CASCADE — so it sees the migrated rows at B. The cache branch is the broken path. Most production syncs hit the cache branch because the integration prefetch is enabled by default.

## Suggested fix

Either:

**(a)** After the integration `id` rewrite at line 1780, refresh the schema cache from the DB before the loop:
```python
existing_cs_result = await self.db.execute(
    select(IntegrationConfigSchema).where(
        IntegrationConfigSchema.integration_id == integ_id
    )
)
existing_cs_by_key = {cs.key: cs for cs in existing_cs_result.scalars().all()}
```

**(b)** When `existing_by_name` triggers an id rewrite, also rewrite the cache key:
```python
if existing_by_name is not None and existing_by_name != integ_id:
    cache["integ_cs"][integ_id] = cache["integ_cs"].pop(existing_by_name, {})
```

(b) is cheaper (no extra query) but mirrors the FK CASCADE behavior in app code, which is fragile. (a) is one round-trip per integration with a UUID rewrite — usually rare, so the cost is negligible.

## Workaround

Manually align the integration UUID before sync:

```sql
UPDATE integrations SET id = '<manifest-uuid>' WHERE id = '<db-uuid>' AND name = '<name>';
-- FK CASCADE migrates integration_config_schema and integration_mappings
```

Then sync — the by-name match becomes a no-op, the upsert path that triggers the bug isn't taken.

## Real-world incidence

Hit this on 2026-04-29 reconciling a SpireTech dev/prod manifest divergence: dev's `Wordpress` and `Facebook` integrations had locally-generated UUIDs that differed from the manifest UUIDs (auto-generated separately on each env). First sync against dev failed cleanly; the workaround above let the second sync complete.

draft.title: CLI auth: ephemeral sessions + multi-instance support
draft.body:
## Problem

The CLI authenticates against one instance at a time via a single global `~/.bifrost/credentials.json`. Two pain points:

1. **Prod + debug stack collide** — `bifrost login` against a debug stack overwrites the prod token.
2. **Multiple debug stacks can't coexist** — `./debug.sh` already isolates per worktree, but every CLI command reads the one global record.

## Solution (high-level)

Two clearly-separated auth paths:

| Path | Triggered by | Tokens stored where | Use case |
|------|-------------|---------------------|----------|
| **Persistent** | `bifrost login` (browser device-code) | OS keychain, keyed by `api_url`; JSON fallback if no keychain backend | Prod, long-lived staging |
| **Ephemeral** | `bifrost login --email X --password Y --ephemeral` | Nowhere — printed to stdout, captured into `.env` by the caller | Debug stacks |

Multi-instance addressing via `.env` in CWD (already auto-loaded by dotenv).

CLI token resolution: env vars → keychain (by URL) → legacy JSON (lazy-migrated).

## Constraints

- Migration must be non-destructive — the prod token in `~/.bifrost/credentials.json` cannot be lost.
- Ephemeral path refuses MFA-required responses with a clear error; warning printed every invocation.
- Headless Linux (no D-Bus / Secret Service) must fall back to JSON cleanly with a logged warning.
- Cross-platform smoke tests required: dev's Linux + Mac before merge; Windows deferred (warning + fallback).

## Spec

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-cli-auth-ephemeral-sessions-design.md` (commit 541c3143)

## Out of scope

- Named profiles (URLs are unique enough)
- Remote-instance management
- `bifrost poc init` scaffolding
- Replacing the device-code login flow

draft.title: [chore]: Universal {location}/{scope}/{path} model for files SDK + signed-url bug
draft.body:
## Summary

The Files SDK's path resolution is inconsistent across `read`/`write`/`list`/`signed-url`, with `signed-url` being the most visibly broken (hardcoded to `uploads/{scope}/{path}`, no `location` parameter, ignores writes to other locations entirely). Rather than patch `signed-url` in isolation, redesign the file path model so all SDK methods share one resolver.

## Proposed model

Universal path layout:

    {location}/{scope}/{path}

Two kinds of locations:

**Reserved (managed):** platform-controlled, not freeform.
- `workspace` → `_repo/{path}` — the platform codebase. **Not scoped** (it's conceptually a git repo, intentionally cross-org). Reject any write/signed-url operation if `_repo/.git/` exists in the bucket — editing a git-controlled workspace is dangerous and should be opt-in if needed at all.
- `uploads` → `uploads/{scope}/{path}` — form uploads and user data.
- `temp` → `_tmp/{scope}/{path}` — ephemeral scratch.
- `_repo`, `_tmp`, `_apps` — direct prefix names blocked at the SDK to prevent collisions with the resolved layout.

**Freeform (user-defined):** anything else (`reports`, `exports`, `archives`, `customer-data`). Always resolved as `{location}/{scope}/{path}`.

## Scope rules

Scope always applies (with the `workspace` exception above). Resolution goes through `resolve_scope()` (`api/bifrost/_context.py:128`), same as every other scoped SDK module (`tables`, `config`, `knowledge`, `integrations`, `email`):

- Default: current execution context's `org_id`.
- Explicit `scope=` parameter allowed only from provider orgs; otherwise `PermissionError`.
- CLI mode: scope honored as-passed (user JWT carries auth).

No SDK method is unscoped except `workspace` reads/writes.

## Location naming policy

For freeform locations:

- Regex: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` (no slashes, no leading underscores).
- Reserved names blocked: `workspace`, `uploads`, `temp`, `_repo`, `_tmp`, `_apps`.
- Validation lives in the path resolver, applied uniformly across read/write/list/signed-url.

## Single source of truth

Path resolution lives in **one** function used by every endpoint:

```python
def resolve_s3_key(location: str, scope: str | None, path: str) -> str:
    # validate location name, reject traversal, reject reserved-prefix paths, then:
    if location == "workspace":
        # caller also checks _repo/.git/ existence and rejects writes if present
        return f"_repo/{path}"
    if location == "uploads":
        return f"uploads/{scope}/{path}"
    if location == "temp":
        return f"_tmp/{scope}/{path}"
    return f"{location}/{scope}/{path}"  # freeform
```

`read`, `write`, `list`, `delete`, `exists`, `signed-url` all call this.

## Form uploads — open question

Forms today write to `uploads/{form_id}/{uuid}/{filename}` (see `api/src/routers/forms.py:1132`), **without scope**. This collides with the proposed `uploads/{scope}/{path}` model.

Options:

1. **Migrate forms under scope:** `uploads/{scope}/{form_id}/{uuid}/{filename}`. Cleaner, but requires backfill of existing form upload references and any persisted form values that hold `uploads/...` paths.
2. **Carve `uploads/forms/` as the form sub-prefix** with the rest of `uploads/` becoming `uploads/{scope}/...`. No backfill but uglier.
3. **Forms write to `uploads/{scope}/{form_id}/{uuid}/{filename}` going forward, leave existing data in place** until natural expiry / manual cleanup. Pragmatic.

Decision needed before implementation. Recommendation: option 3 if form upload references are short-lived (most are), option 1 if they're durable.

## Migration surface

Code touching the current path layout:

- `api/bifrost/files.py` — every SDK method, add `location` to `get_signed_url`, route through new resolver.
- `api/src/routers/files.py` — replace inline `s3_path = ...` in `get_signed_url` (line 340), `read_file`, etc., with resolver calls.
- `api/src/services/file_backend.py` (cloud backend) — `_resolve_path` becomes a thin wrapper over the new resolver; remove duplicate `_repo/`, `_tmp/`, `uploads/` mappings.
- `api/src/routers/forms.py` (lines 1072, 1132) — depends on form-uploads decision above.
- `RESERVED_PREFIXES` in signed-url handler — folded into the resolver's validation.

## Original signed-url bug (now a sub-task)

`files.get_signed_url(path, ...)` returns a URL targeting `uploads/{scope}/{path}` regardless of where the file actually lives. Files written via `files.write_bytes(..., location="workspace")` go to `_repo/{path}`, so the signed URL returns S3 `NoSuchKey`. This bug disappears once `signed-url` uses the shared resolver and accepts a `location` parameter.

Reproduction:

```python
@workflow
async def repro() -> dict:
    path = "demo/hello.pdf"
    await files.write_bytes(path, b"...", location="workspace")
    return await files.get_signed_url(path, method="GET")  # NoSuchKey
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single `resolve_s3_key(location, scope, path)` function used by every files endpoint.
- [ ] `files.get_signed_url(path, location=..., scope=...)` — same signature shape as `read`/`write`.
- [ ] Round-trip test: `write_bytes(path, b"...", location=L)` → `get_signed_url(path, method="GET", location=L)` → HTTP fetch → bytes match. Run for `workspace`, `uploads`, `temp`, and a freeform location.
- [ ] Scope override across orgs requires provider context (existing `resolve_scope` behavior, but now applied to files).
- [ ] `workspace` writes/signed-urls rejected when `_repo/.git/` exists in the bucket.
- [ ] Freeform location names validated against name regex; reserved names rejected.
- [ ] Form upload migration decision documented and applied.
- [ ] CLI/MCP equivalents (`bifrost files ...`) updated for new `location` semantics.

draft.title: RFC: Add durable webhook inbox for reliable event ingestion and replay
draft.body:
## Summary
Introduce a durable webhook inbox layer for Bifrost's event system so inbound webhooks are persisted immediately, processed asynchronously by workers, and safely replayable/retriable when downstream validation, event routing, delivery creation, or workflow queueing fails.
The goal is not to replace the existing event/workflow queue architecture. It is to strengthen the edge of the system by treating external webhooks as unreliable ingress signals and converting them into durable internal records before doing meaningful application work.
## Problem
Webhooks are not a delivery guarantee. Even when delivered over HTTPS/TCP, they are usually only a best-effort HTTP request from a vendor. Vendor retry semantics vary, ordering is not guaranteed, and many providers provide limited or no replay capability.
Today, Bifrost already has strong internal async execution primitives:
- RabbitMQ for async workflow execution.
- Worker consumers for queued workflow/agent work.
- Event and EventDelivery records for normalized platform events and subscription delivery tracking.
- Postgres as the durable system of record.
However, the webhook request path appears to do meaningful work synchronously before returning to the vendor:

```text
/api/hooks/{source_id}
  -> read raw body
  -> route through webhook adapter
  -> validate/parse/normalize request
  -> create Event + EventDelivery rows
  -> commit
  -> queue workflow/agent deliveries
  -> return 202

This is already better than direct webhook execution, but it still leaves reliability gaps:

1. If adapter validation/parsing, DB writes, or delivery queueing has a transient failure, the vendor may or may not retry.
2. If the event is recorded but delivery queueing fails, Bifrost needs an explicit recovery path for pending/stuck deliveries.
3. Raw webhook payloads are not clearly modeled as first-class durable ingress records that can be replayed, audited, deduplicated, or reprocessed after code changes.
4. The boundary between external webhook receipt and internal event processing is not as strong as it could be.

Proposal

Add a first-class WebhookInbox model and processing pipeline.

The webhook receiver should do as little as possible:

Webhook received
  -> minimal source lookup
  -> optional cheap adapter pre-check if required
  -> write WebhookInbox row with raw request envelope
  -> commit
  -> enqueue webhook-inbox processing message
  -> return 202 Accepted

A worker then processes the inbox record asynchronously:

WebhookInbox worker
  -> load raw inbox row
  -> run adapter validation/parsing/normalization
  -> create Event row
  -> create EventDelivery rows
  -> queue workflow/agent executions
  -> mark inbox processed/rejected/failed

A scheduled reconciler should recover stuck work:

periodic reconciler
  -> find WebhookInbox rows stuck in received/processing
  -> find EventDelivery rows stuck in pending/queued without execution
  -> retry safely with idempotency controls

Proposed data model

A rough webhook_inbox table:

id uuid primary key
source_id uuid not null
webhook_source_id uuid nullable
adapter_name text nullable
method text not null
path text not null
headers jsonb not null
query_params jsonb not null
body bytea or text/blob reference not null
body_sha256 text not null
source_ip text nullable
received_at timestamptz not null
status text not null -- received | processing | processed | rejected | failed | dead_lettered
attempt_count integer not null default 0
next_attempt_at timestamptz nullable
locked_at timestamptz nullable
locked_by text nullable
provider_event_id text nullable
idempotency_key text nullable
normalized_event_id uuid nullable
last_error text nullable
last_error_type text nullable
processed_at timestamptz nullable
created_at timestamptz not null
updated_at timestamptz not null

Notes:

* Store the raw request envelope before adapter processing.
* For large bodies, consider storing body content in object storage and only keeping a reference + hash in Postgres.
* Add unique constraints where reliable provider event IDs exist.
* Preserve headers/body sufficiently for signature validation and replay.
* Redact or avoid displaying sensitive headers in the UI, but keep enough raw material for validation and forensic replay.

Proposed queue

Add a new RabbitMQ queue, for example:

webhook-inbox-processing

Message shape:

{
  "inbox_id": "uuid",
  "source_id": "uuid"
}

The queue message should be treated as a dispatch hint. The canonical state should remain the WebhookInbox row.

Retry and idempotency behavior

The worker should be idempotent:

* If WebhookInbox.status = processed, skip.
* If the inbox row already has normalized_event_id, do not create a duplicate Event.
* If provider event IDs are available, deduplicate per source/provider event ID.
* If no provider event ID exists, use a best-effort key such as (source_id, body_sha256, received time window) only where safe.
* Delivery queueing should be retryable without duplicating executions.

Retries should distinguish:

* rejected: adapter says invalid signature, wrong challenge, unsupported event, etc. Usually terminal.
* failed: transient or internal processing failure. Retryable.
* dead_lettered: retry budget exceeded or manual intervention required.

Reconciliation

Add a scheduler job or platform maintenance task that periodically checks for:

1. WebhookInbox rows in received that were never queued.
2. WebhookInbox rows stuck in processing past a lease timeout.
3. EventDelivery rows in pending that were never queued.
4. EventDelivery rows in queued without corresponding execution/agent run after a threshold.

This reconciler is the real reliability win: RabbitMQ can dispatch, but Postgres should remain the source of truth for what was accepted and what still needs work.

UI / operator experience

Eventually expose an operator-facing view for webhook ingress:

* Raw received time.
* Source / adapter.
* Status.
* Attempt count.
* Linked Event.
* Linked EventDelivery records.
* Linked workflow execution or agent run.
* Last error.
* Manual actions:
    * retry processing
    * mark rejected
    * dead-letter
    * replay into event system

This would make webhook ingestion auditable in the same spirit as workflow executions.

Security considerations

* Webhook endpoints remain unauthenticated at the platform auth layer, but protected by UUID callback paths and adapter-specific validation.
* Preserve raw body bytes exactly for HMAC validation.
* Do not log full raw bodies or sensitive headers.
* Redact common sensitive headers in UI/API responses.
* Consider retention controls for raw webhook data.
* Consider size limits and content-type handling before writing raw bodies.
* Consider per-source rate limits to avoid inbox flooding.

Incremental implementation plan

Phase 1: Durable inbox foundation

* Add WebhookInbox ORM model and migration.
* Add repository methods for create, lease, status update, and retry queries.
* Modify /api/hooks/{source_id} to persist raw request envelope and return 202 after enqueueing inbox processing.
* Preserve existing validation/handshake behavior where providers require a synchronous response.

Phase 2: Inbox worker

* Add WebhookInboxConsumer on a new RabbitMQ queue.
* Move adapter processing + Event/EventDelivery creation into the worker path.
* Ensure queue message only references inbox_id.
* Preserve existing EventProcessor behavior behind a service method so current logic is reused rather than forked.

Phase 3: Reconciler and retry controls

* Add scheduled reconciliation for stuck inbox rows and pending deliveries.
* Add retry budget/backoff.
* Add dead-letter state.
* Add idempotency protections.

Phase 4: UI/API observability

* Add platform/admin endpoints for listing inbox records.
* Link inbox records to Event, EventDelivery, Execution, and AgentRun records.
* Add manual retry/dead-letter actions.

Compatibility notes

Some webhook providers require synchronous challenge/validation responses, especially during webhook registration. Those flows may need to remain adapter-handled in the request path.

Suggested split:

validation/challenge request
  -> adapter returns ValidationResponse synchronously
delivery request
  -> persist to WebhookInbox
  -> process asynchronously

Acceptance criteria

* Inbound delivery webhooks are durably recorded before meaningful processing.
* The webhook endpoint returns quickly after durable acceptance.
* Raw payloads can be replayed/reprocessed by ID.
* Worker processing is idempotent.
* Delivery queueing can be retried without creating duplicate workflow executions.
* Stuck inbox rows and pending deliveries are automatically reconciled.
* Operators can determine: received payload -> normalized event -> delivery -> execution/result.
* Existing webhook adapter behavior continues to work, including validation/challenge flows.

Why this matters

This would make Bifrost’s webhook/event system more durable and operationally trustworthy for MSP automation use cases.

For things like RMM events, network alerts, security alerts, customer-facing automations, and vendor integrations, the desired posture should be:

We accepted the webhook.
We can prove exactly what we received.
We can show how it was normalized.
We can show what matched.
We can show what ran.
We can retry or replay safely.

In short: webhooks should be an ingress mechanism, not the delivery guarantee. Bifrost should convert them into durable, replayable internal events.

draft.title: [chore]: remove workspace .git/ write gate from files endpoints
draft.body:
## Summary

PR #155 added a server-side gate that rejects `POST /api/files/write` and `POST /api/files/signed-url` (PUT) when `_repo/.git/` exists, on the premise that a git-controlled workspace shouldn't accept writes that aren't going through `bifrost git`.

The gate is too broad: `bifrost watch`, `bifrost sync`/`push`, `bifrost import`, and the web code editor (existing) and web SDK files API (planned) all hit those endpoints with legitimate workspace writes. Watch in particular is fully blocked against any workspace that's been bootstrapped via `bifrost git`.

The protection the gate was after — "don't clobber a pending `bifrost git pull`" — is already enforced by `bifrost git` itself, which refuses to merge over a dirty `_repo/`. The data-plane gate is a duplicate guard.

## Changes

- Remove `_is_workspace_git_locked()` and both gate sites in `api/src/routers/files.py` (write_file ~line 209, get_signed_url ~line 351).
- Drop `TestWorkspaceGitLock` from `api/tests/unit/routers/test_files_signed_url.py`.
- Drop the `pytest.skip("workspace is git-controlled; ...")` branch in `api/tests/e2e/api/test_files_signed_url_roundtrip.py:49`.

## Out of scope

- A future "this workspace is git-controlled" warning surfaced by `bifrost watch` startup and the web code editor — separate change once we have a concrete UX for it.

draft.title: [feature]: CLI access controls for workflows/forms (organization, access_level, roles) on create/update + skill guidance
draft.body:
## Summary

When developing apps via the SDK/CLI, contributors can't fully assign access (organization, access level, roles) at create/update time. This forces users into the UI for what should be a scriptable, reproducible workflow — and there's no skill-level prompt to remind us to plan compatible access across an app and its supporting workflows/forms.

## Current state (audit)

| Surface | `organization_id` | `access_level` | Roles | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bifrost workflows register` | `--org` only | ❌ | ❌ | Have to register, then `update`, then `grant-role` per role |
| `bifrost workflows update` | ✅ | ✅ | `--clear-roles` + per-role `grant-role` / `revoke-role` | No bulk `--role-ids a,b,c` apply |
| `bifrost forms create` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ no `role_ids` on `FormCreate`; ❌ no `/forms/{id}/roles` endpoint | **Cannot assign form roles via CLI at all** |
| `bifrost forms update` | ✅ | ✅ | `--clear-roles` only | Same |
| `bifrost apps create/update` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ `--role-ids` (accepts names) | Already complete — use as the reference pattern |

References:
- `api/src/models/contracts/applications.py:41-107` — `ApplicationCreate` / `ApplicationUpdate` already carry `access_level` + `role_ids`.
- `api/src/models/contracts/forms.py:260-288` — `FormCreate` / `FormUpdate` are missing `role_ids`.
- `api/src/models/contracts/workflows.py:261` — `WorkflowUpdateRequest` has `clear_roles` but no `role_ids` for bulk apply.
- `api/bifrost/commands/workflows.py:111-156` — `register` only accepts `--org`.
- `api/bifrost/commands/forms.py:93-142` — generic create/update, no role surface.
- `api/bifrost/dto_flags.py:103-126` — `FormCreate` ref-lookups already include `organization_id`; need a `role_ids` rule too once the DTO field exists.

## Proposed scope

**Workflows**
- `bifrost workflows register`: add `--access-level`, `--role-ids` (comma-split, name-or-UUID).
- Add `role_ids: list[UUID] | None` to `WorkflowUpdateRequest` so `bifrost workflows update --role-ids …` does a bulk replace (current `--clear-roles` + `grant-role`-per-role flow stays as the per-role primitive).

**Forms**
- Add `role_ids: list[UUID] | None` to `FormCreate` and `FormUpdate`.
- Server-side: persist via `FormRoleORM` (same table the read path at `api/src/routers/forms.py:424` already uses).
- DTO ref-lookup in `dto_flags.py` so `--role-ids finance,billing` resolves to UUIDs (mirrors apps).

**Apps**
- No code change needed; surface is complete. Mention as the reference pattern in the skill.

**`bifrost-build` skill**
- Add an "access compatibility" checkpoint to the SKILL.md scaffolding flow:

  > **Confirm who should have access before scaffolding.** When building an app, plan compatible access across its workflows and forms. Example: a Finance app assigned to the `finance` role with workflows under Organization A. Supporting workflows must either be (a) global, (b) scoped to the same organization for authenticated users, or (c) assigned the same role(s) as the app — otherwise users with the app role won't be able to execute the workflows it depends on. Ask the user once, capture the access tuple `(organization, access_level, role_ids)`, and pass it through every subsequent `register` / `create` call.

**Tests**
- DTO-parity via `tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py` will catch the new fields automatically (or require `DTO_EXCLUDES` entries with rationale).
- Unit tests for `assemble_body` resolving `--role-ids` for forms and workflows.
- E2E in `tests/e2e/api/test_forms.py` covering form-create-with-roles and form-update-with-roles.

## Out of scope

- Adding `POST/DELETE /api/forms/{id}/roles` endpoints (workflows-style per-role primitive). Bulk `role_ids` on the DTO is sufficient for now.
- UI changes to the access editor.
- Reworking the workflow `grant-role` / `revoke-role` per-role endpoints — they stay as the precision primitive; bulk `--role-ids` is additive.
- Any access changes to agents / tables / configs / events (file separately if those have the same gap).

## Notes

- `bifrost apps` is the gold-standard pattern here — `role_ids` on the DTO with `--role-ids` resolved to UUIDs by `dto_flags.py:461-465`. Mirror that shape for workflows + forms.
- This is also a portability concern: forms exported via `bifrost export --portable` lose role assignments today because the manifest entry has nowhere to put them. Adding `role_ids` to the DTO closes the round-trip.
